dedupe_keys.name: infrarisk simulation platform for resilience of interdependent power water and transport networks

description: InfraRisk is an open-source Python package that simulates disaster-induced failures and post-disaster restoration in interconnected water, power and road networks at asset level. It couples existing network packages, wntr for water, pandapower for power and a static traffic assignment model for roads, through an interface for interdependent failures, and adds a hazard module that generates component failure sequences, a recovery module that assigns repair crews by heuristic strategies or model predictive control optimisation, a simulation module and a resilience module with system-level and consumer-level metrics. It was developed at the Singapore-ETH Centre and published in Sustainable Cities and Society in 2022; two testbeds ship with it, a simple network and a modified Micropolis virtual city of 5,000 inhabitants, used in the paper for 165 hypothetical flood events. The code is accessible on GitHub under the MIT licence and installs with conda or pip; it is free. Caveats: the testbeds are synthetic, flood failure probabilities in the demonstration are assumed, and real use needs the user's own network models. It supports cascading failure, restoration and resilience simulation for pre- and post-disaster policy testing; related records are WNTR, pandapower and IN-CORE.
